## Consolidated Findings

- product/requirements/FR-CCEF-025.md: Display name character validation is too restrictive for international names. Excludes diacritical marks (é, ñ, ü, ç), accented characters common in Swedish (å, ä, ö), and non-Latin scripts. This creates an accessibility and internationalization gap that will cause validation failures for users with non-ASCII names.
- product/requirements/FR-CCEF-031.md: Scroll-to-bottom requirement for legal acceptance is a known UX anti-pattern. It adds unnecessary friction, may confuse users unfamiliar with the pattern, and creates accessibility barriers for screen reader users (who cannot visually confirm scroll position) and users with motor impairments. Consider replacing with a simple checkbox that is always enabled.
- product/requirements/FR-CCEF-031.md: SSO user interaction with legal acceptance is not clearly specified. Users authenticating via Google SSO (FR-CCEF-001) or Apple SSO (FR-CCEF-002) may skip the account creation flow entirely, but it is unclear whether they encounter legal acceptance during SSO login, as a separate step, or only when creating an email+password account. This ambiguity could lead to inconsistent consent collection.
- product/requirements/FR-CCEF-028.md: Input validation requirement does not specify assistive technology communication. Real-time validation errors should be announced via ARIA live regions and focus management for screen reader users, but this is not specified. This could create accessibility gaps in the account settings forms.
- product/requirements/NFR-CCEF-003.md: Rate limiting NFR does not specify user-facing UX for rate-limited interactions. Users who exceed OTP resend limits or login attempt thresholds need clear, non-technical feedback about why their action was blocked and when they can retry. Without this specification, implementers may use inconsistent or confusing error messages.
- product/architectural-decisions/ADR-0002-gdpr-compliant-data-handling.md: Consent withdrawal mechanism is mentioned as a GDPR constraint but no user-facing UX specification exists. Users need a clear, accessible way to withdraw consent after initial acceptance (e.g., from account settings). Without this specification, the system may not fully support GDPR Article 7(3) right to withdraw consent.

## Required Changes

None.

## Suggested Changes

- product/requirements/FR-CCEF-025.md: Relax display name character validation to support Unicode letters (including diacritical marks and non-Latin scripts). At minimum, include Swedish characters å, ä, ö. Consider using a Unicode letter category check (e.g., \p{L} in regex) instead of restricting to ASCII a-z, A-Z.
- product/requirements/FR-CCEF-031.md: Replace scroll-to-bottom requirement with a simple always-enabled checkbox. If tracking document engagement is important, log that the user viewed the document (e.g., time spent on page) without making it a gate to acceptance.
- product/requirements/FR-CCEF-031.md: Clarify how SSO-authenticated users (Google/Apple) encounter legal acceptance. Specify whether it is presented during initial SSO login, as a post-SSO onboarding step for new users, or only during email+password account creation. Ensure consistent consent collection across all auth methods.
- product/requirements/FR-CCEF-028.md: Add accessibility specification for validation error communication: errors should be announced via ARIA live regions, focus should move to the first invalid field on submit failure, and error messages should be programmatically associated with their fields using aria-describedby.
- product/requirements/NFR-CCEF-003.md: Add user-facing UX specification for rate-limited interactions: clear error messages explaining the limit, time until retry is available, and prevention of repeated failed attempts. This applies to OTP resend throttling, login attempt limits, and any other rate-limited flows.
- product/requirements/FR-CCEF-006.md: Add user-facing UX specification for consent withdrawal: provide an accessible mechanism in account settings (or a dedicated privacy page) where users can withdraw previously given consent for personal data processing, with clear confirmation and explanation of consequences.
- product/requirements/FR-CCEF-026.md: While immediate language switching is a good UX goal, specify how partial translations are handled during the transition. If some UI elements lack Swedish translations, define the fallback behavior (e.g., show English with a visual indicator) to avoid confusing users during the switch.
